children.title: Project Management Practices
children.summary: Defined policies and procedures used to plan, execute, and control IS projects.

children.title: Project Management Structure
children.summary: Organizational framework defining how project teams interact and report.

children.title: Project Management Roles and Responsibility
children.summary: Clear definition of duties for all personnel involved in the project.

children.title: Project Management Techniques
children.summary: Tools and methods like PERT, Gantt charts, or critical path analysis.

children.title: Portfolio/Program Management
children.summary: Oversight of multiple related projects (program) or strategic selection of projects (portfolio).

children.title: Project Management Office
children.summary: Centralized department that standardizes project governance and processes.

children.title: Project Benefit Realization
children.summary: Ensuring the project delivers the intended business value and measurable outcomes.

children.title: Project Initiation
children.summary: The formal process of starting a new project or phase.

children.title: Project Objectives
children.summary: Specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound goals for the project.

children.title: Project Planning
children.summary: Developing the project management plan, scope, schedule, and resource allocation.

children.title: Schedule Development
children.summary: The process of determining task sequences and durations.

children.title: Gantt Chart Creation (L4 Example)
children.summary: A specific tool used for visualizing the project timeline and dependencies.

children.title: Project Execution
children.summary: Carrying out the planned tasks and producing the deliverables.

children.title: Project Controlling and Monitoring
children.summary: Tracking, reviewing, and regulating the progress and performance of the project.

children.title: Project Closing
children.summary: Formal completion of the project, including delivery, review, and documentation.

children.title: Project Scope
children.summary: The boundaries and limits of the project, defining what is and is not included.

children.title: Current Analysis
children.summary: Assessment of the existing system or process to identify weaknesses and opportunities.

children.title: Requirements
children.summary: Detailed needs and constraints that the new system must satisfy (functional and non-functional).

children.title: Approach
children.summary: The planned method or strategy for system development (e.g., in-house, purchase, outsourcing).

children.title: Evaluation
children.summary: Analyzing costs, benefits, and risks across different solution alternatives.

children.title: Review
children.summary: Formal assessment of the business case before approval to proceed.

children.title: Business Application Development
children.summary: The process of creating software or applications to meet specific business needs.

children.title: SDLC Models
children.summary: Different frameworks for system development, such as Waterfall, Agile, or V-model.

children.title: SDLC Phases
children.summary: Sequential steps in the System Development Life Cycle (e.g., Planning, Analysis, Design, Implementation, Maintenance).

children.title: Software Development Methods
children.summary: Specific techniques used in coding and testing, like object-oriented programming or structured programming.

children.title: System Development Tools and Productivity Aids
children.summary: CASE tools, code generators, debuggers, and other tools that enhance development efficiency.

children.title: Infrastructure Development/Acquisition Practices
children.summary: The process of planning, designing, and acquiring the necessary hardware, network, and operating systems.

children.title: Hardware/Software Acquisition
children.summary: Procedures for procurement, testing, and implementation of new technology components.

children.title: System Software Acquisition
children.summary: Acquiring operating systems, database management systems, and other foundational software.

children.title: Input/Origination Controls
children.summary: Controls ensuring data is accurately captured and authorized at the source (e.g., validation checks, sequence checks).

children.title: Processing Procedures and Controls
children.summary: Controls ensuring data is correctly processed (e.g., batch totals, cross-footing, limit checks).

children.title: Output Controls
children.summary: Controls ensuring output is accurate, secure, and delivered only to authorized recipients (e.g., review procedures, reconciliation).

children.title: Application Controls
children.summary: Controls embedded within the application software itself to ensure data integrity and security (e.g., access controls, audit trails).

children.title: User Procedures
children.summary: Manual steps and policies users follow to operate the system securely and correctly.

children.title: Decision Support System
children.summary: System designed to support decision-making activities, often requiring specific controls over data quality and models.
